question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two independent continuous random variables whose marginal density functions are as follows:

$$
{f}_{X}(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{8}x, & \,0\le x\le 4, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}\,\,{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{5}y, & \,2\le y\le 3, \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(1\le X\le 2,1\le Y\le 3).$
question.worked_solution:
Two continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability density functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Since our random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}x\cdot \frac{2}{5}y \\  & =\frac{1}{20}xy,\end{aligned}
$$

where $(x,y)\in [0,4]\times [2,3].$ Therefore, the full expression for $f(x,y)$ is

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{20}xy, & \,0\le x\le 4,\,2\le y\le 3 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le X\le 2,1\le Y\le 3) & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{1}{20}xy\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{20}x{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{2}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{8}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{16}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(2)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(1)^{2}}{16} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
